findings.summary: The home link's aria-label "Homepage" replaces the visible name "WaterLevels.org", so speech input and screen readers never hear the brand text on screen.
findings.fix: Remove aria-label from the brand link. The visible span.name is already the accessible name, and the mark is aria-hidden. Do not add role="link".

findings.summary: Flood alerts and state directory pages render a second header next to the site header, so assistive technology exposes two banners and the h1 is outside main.
findings.fix: Change header.state-hero to a div and place it inside main so there is one banner and the h1 is in the main landmark. Apply the same change at app/views/states/show.html.erb:20.

findings.summary: Terms (20), privacy (14), disclosures (8), AUP (4), and about (3) sections with aria-labelledby are region landmarks, so the landmark list repeats headings the H key already reaches.
findings.fix: Remove aria-labelledby from those sections and keep the h2 elements. Leave a section unlabeled unless it is a destination beyond heading navigation.

findings.summary: The home stats, trends, and popular blocks are named regions. The stats strip is not a destination, and the other two are already reachable from their h2s.
findings.fix: Remove aria-labelledby from home-stats, home-trends, and home-popular and keep the h2 elements. Use a div for the stats strip so it is not a region landmark.

findings.summary: The interactive Leaflet map is forced to role="img", which treats a keyboard-focusable map as one image and hides descendant controls such as the attribution links.
findings.fix: Remove role="img" from the canvas. Name the map surface with role="region" and a label, and leave Leaflet attribution as real links. Do not rely on a hidden settings list as the only text alternative.

findings.summary: The stations-in-view status live region sits inside the hidden settings aside, so pan and filter updates are not announced while that panel is closed.
findings.fix: Move the role="status" node outside #map-settings-panel so it stays exposed. Keep updating its textContent, and do not leave the only keyboard station list inside a hidden panel.

findings.summary: The map search button has no aria-expanded state and no aria-controls target, so screen readers cannot tell that it opens or closes the full-screen search.
findings.fix: Set aria-expanded="false" and aria-controls="map-mobile-search" on the button, and id="map-mobile-search" on the panel. Toggle aria-expanded in openMobileSearch and closeMobileSearch the way settings already does.

findings.summary: Closing map search or settings hides the focused close button or field and does not return focus to the opener, so keyboard focus is lost.
findings.fix: Before setting hidden, if document.activeElement is inside the panel, focus the search toggle or the settings button. Do this for the in-panel close buttons and for Escape.
findings.evidence: closeMobileSearch() sets mobileSearchTarget.hidden = true and does not call focus() on the opener.

findings.summary: Search suggestions are tabbable links with role="option", and the home listbox also contains a browse link that is not an option, so the tab order and the listbox model disagree.
findings.fix: Render suggestions as non-focusable role="option" nodes and activate the active option from the input. Move the browse link outside #home-search-results. Use the same option markup in map_controller.js searchResultItemHtml.
findings.evidence: <a href="…" class="item" role="option"> inside role="listbox", plus a footer <a> with no option role.

findings.summary: Enter on the map combobox submits the first result while arrow keys expose a different option, and aria-activedescendant is left pointing at a removed id after the list is rebuilt.
findings.fix: In one Enter handler, activate the option at searchActiveIndex when it is set; otherwise submit the first match. In renderSearchResults, remove aria-activedescendant whenever the list is replaced or hidden.
findings.evidence: keydown.enter->map#submitSearch always uses searchResults[0]; renderSearchResults does not clear aria-activedescendant.

findings.summary: The home and map search fields have no visible label. The placeholder disappears while typing, and the name is only aria-label "Search stations".
findings.fix: Add a visible <label for="home-search-input">Search stations</label> and the same for #map-search-input. Remove the duplicate aria-label so the accessible name comes from the label.
findings.evidence: <input type="search" id="home-search-input" role="combobox" aria-label="Search stations" placeholder="Search by station name…">

findings.summary: Station name and details are adjacent flex items inside one link, with only a gap between them, so the link name can be spoken with no word boundary.
findings.fix: Put the name and meta spans in one flex child and include a real separator in the text, such as a comma inside the meta span. Apply that to popular links, home/_trend_rows.html.erb, map station-list links, and suggestion rows whose status is a sibling flex item.

findings.summary: The honeypot helper randomly positions the decoy field off-screen instead of using display:none, so screen readers can reach a field that silently discards the submission.
findings.fix: Do not use Invisible Captcha's random css_strategy. Put the honeypot in a container with the hidden attribute so it is out of the accessibility tree on every request. The same helper is at app/views/subscriptions/new.html.erb:29.
findings.evidence: css_strategy samples display:none, top:-9999px, or a 1px clip. The field label is "If you are a human, ignore this field".

findings.summary: The map page has no h1. Its only headings are h2s inside the collapsed settings and search panels, so heading navigation never names the page.
findings.fix:
Add an h1 in main before the canvas, for example

Water level map

, and keep the panel headings at h2.
findings.evidence: <main id="main" class="map-main"> has h2 "Data layers" and h2 "Search stations" only.

findings.summary: On About, FAQ, and Data disclosures the h1 is in a section before main, so skip-to-main and the main landmark both skip the page title.
findings.fix: Move each page-hero section inside main, including the h1. Do not give the hero a landmark name. The same split is at faq.html.erb:21 and disclosures.html.erb:16.

findings.summary: The directory filter aside, the FAQ sidebar, and the map settings aside have no accessible name, so landmark navigation announces them only as complementary.
findings.fix: Name each aside from its visible heading with aria-labelledby: "Filters" on the directory aside, "Categories" on the FAQ aside, and the "Data layers" h2 on #map-settings-panel. Do not add a mismatched aria-label.
findings.evidence: <aside class="filter-panel"> and <aside class="faq-sidebar"> and <aside id="map-settings-panel" hidden>

passed: No div or span controls with role=button, and no role=button on button elements.
Mobile navigation uses a button with aria-expanded, aria-controls pointing at #mobile-primary-nav, display:none when closed, focus moved into the panel, and focus returned to the toggle on Escape.
Primary, mobile, footer, and FAQ navs have distinct accessible names. Current links use aria-current=page.
Skip link targets #main, and each in-scope page has one main element.
FAQ answers are buttons inside h3 elements. aria-expanded updates, aria-controls and aria-labelledby resolve, and only one panel is open.
Map settings aria-expanded updates and aria-controls points at #map-settings-panel. Zoom, locate, and close buttons are named and their icons are aria-hidden.
Legend and county jump use native details and summary. Directory groups are unlabeled sections with h2s, not extra regions.
Home combobox aria-expanded and aria-activedescendant are cleared when the list closes. State directory search has a visible label, and its status live region is not inside a hidden panel.
Contact fields use label for/id, required, and aria-invalid plus aria-describedby only when the matching error element is rendered. The subscription email field has a matching label.
Dialog aria-labelledby and aria-describedby ids exist in the dialog component. Template aria-controls, aria-labelledby, and aria-describedby references resolve.
Decorative icons, glow blobs, and legend swatches are aria-hidden. Icon-only header and map buttons have accessible names.
notes: Source review only. Live-region speech, Safari flex-item name calculation, and whether aria-modal keeps virtual focus inside the div dialog without inert were not run in a browser.

The geolocation dialog meets the custom dialog checklist (role, aria-modal, label, description, Tab trap, Escape, focus return) but is a div, not a native dialog, and the controller never sets inert on the rest of the page.
FAQ category buttons update aria-current and do not use tab roles or aria-controls. That fits a button group because arrow-key tab selection is not implemented.
Directory and map checkbox groups use role=group with an aria-label that matches the nearby text. A fieldset and legend would name them without ARIA; the current names are not broken references.

Contact and subscription failures re-render a flash role=alert, and contact field errors use aria-describedby. Focus is not moved to the first invalid control. Whether the initial alert is announced on load was not runtime-tested.
The Turnstile wrapper aria-label is on a generic div, which browsers ignore. The injected iframe title is not in these templates.
Map station search and its opener are both hidden from the md breakpoint up, so desktop has no search combobox for any input method.
Alert and state temperature values are empty until temperature_unit_controller fills them. Those pages do not render the aria-pressed unit buttons.
Prose ul role=list repeats the implicit list role. Those lists use list-disc, so this is not a list-style:none repair and was not treated as a double announcement.
